title: SLO Windows, Reservation Guarantees, and Isolation Policies for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Priya Shah
description: Goal: Define product requirements for predictable, contract-grade Dedicated capacity behavior across time-bound SLO windows, reservation guarantees, and tenant isolation controls. This PRD covers the user-facing reservation semantics (reservation vs. burst vs. best-effort), SLO windows for latency and throughput guarantees, preemption and spillover policies, and admin controls for isolation zones and cross-tenant placement. It focuses on features required for enterprise contracts that demand predictable throughput and explicit isolation guarantees while enabling controlled temporary burst behavior for short-term spikes.
goals: Provide explicit reservation semantics: Customers can reserve capacity with a contractual baseline throughput (qps/tokens/sec) and max concurrency guarantees.
Introduce SLO windows: allow customers to define time-bound SLOs (e.g., business hours, night batch) that change reservation weight and billing multipliers.
Implement tenant isolation zones: support logical isolation settings (soft vs hard) that affect preemption and colocated workloads.
Define burst and preemption policies: allow configurable burst allowance with clear precedence rules and preemptive displacement policies for best-effort workloads.
Expose controls for platform and customer admins: console/APIs for configuring reservations, SLO windows, and isolation settings and visibility into guarantee compliance.
Maintain strong observability: metrics, SLA reports, and audit logs to demonstrate delivered vs contracted guarantees.
non_goals: Full redesign of existing autoscaler internals (this will iterate separately with Eng team).
Pricing redesign outside introducing billing multipliers tied to SLO windows. Detailed commercial contract language handled by Sales/Legal.
On-prem packaging changes; Private mode compatibility will be validated but heavy install changes are out of scope.
success_metrics: Customer-facing SLA reports available for reserved capacity within release quarter.
<95% of customer reservations meet baseline throughput and latency SLO during defined SLO windows over 30-day rolling window.
Reduction in post-deployment capacity-related support escalations for Dedicated customers by 40% in Q2 following release.
Customers can configure SLO windows and reservations via Console/API; 80% of targeted pilot customers adopt SLO windows in pilot phase.
assumptions: Serving runtime can surface tenant-level capacity metrics (qps, tokens/sec, avg latency) with 1s resolution.
Existing dedicated pool primitives (GPU pools, node groups) can be extended with reservation metadata without full infra changes.
Billing system can accept a simple multiplier input per reservation for SLO window billing adjustments in the current quarter.
requirements: REQ-1: Reservation API - Customers can create/update/delete reservations with fields: baseline_throughput, max_concurrency, start_time, end_time, time_zone, billing_multiplier, isolation_mode.
REQ-2: SLO Window Definition - Support recurring windows (cron-like), one-off windows, and overrides for holidays with validation in Console.
REQ-3: Isolation Modes - 'soft' (preferential scheduling, may be preempted by higher-tier reservations) and 'hard' (strict non-preemption unless customer explicitly allows).
REQ-4: Preemption Policy Engine - Deterministic precedence rules by reservation priority, age, and isolation_mode; implement graceful eviction with user-facing reason codes.
REQ-5: Burst Allowance - Configurable burst budget (tokens/minute or concurrency buffer) with guardrails and automatic decay to prevent runaway costs.
REQ-6: Admission & Routing - Smart router must respect reservation windows and isolation when routing requests; fallbacks to compatible model variants when reservation cannot be satisfied.
REQ-7: Console & API UX - Reservation and SLO management UI, on-screen validation, and an audit trail for changes.
REQ-8: Observability - Per-reservation metrics, delivered vs requested throughput, violation counts, and a per-window SLA report exportable as CSV/PDF.
REQ-9: Alerts - Automated alerts to customer and Redwood ops when reservation utilization >110% sustained for X minutes or when preemptions occur above threshold.
REQ-10: Billing Integration - Tag reservation usage with billing_multiplier and ensure meter emits necessary dimensions for invoice reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Reservation creation flow works end-to-end via API and Console and appears in reservation list within 30s.
AC-2: During a defined SLO window, baseline_throughput is honored for 95% of 1-minute slices over a 24h test run under synthetic load matching customer traffic patterns.
AC-3: Isolation 'hard' mode prevents eviction of tenant tasks by other tenant reservations for the duration of the reservation; validated with an integration test that tries to preempt and fails.
AC-4: Burst allowance metrics are emitted and documented; bursts beyond configured budget trigger an alert and throttle per policy.

AC-5: SLA report shows delivered vs contracted metrics and matches internal telemetry for a 7-day window; exported CSV includes reservation id, window, requested throughput, delivered throughput, violations.
AC-6: Preemption events include reason codes, affected request IDs, and are visible in audit logs; ops-runbook links included.
AC-7: Billing records include reservation id and billing_multiplier tag for every hour of reservation activity and reconcile with usage meter within 1% across sample period.
AC-8: Pilot customers (at least 3) complete end-to-end validation and provide sign-off for GA.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal alpha with engineering and 1 pilot customer (2 weeks) focusing on API + telemetry. Phase 2: Expanded pilot with 2 additional enterprise customers and Console UX polish (4 weeks). Phase 3: GA with billing integration and documentation (2 weeks). Feature gates will be used to enable reservations per-org during pilot.
monitoring_and_alerting: Expose metrics: reservation.requested_throughput, reservation.delivered_throughput, reservation.violation_count, reservation.burst_consumed, reservation.preemptions. Alerts: reservation_violation_rate > 5% for 15m; burst_budget_exhausted; preemptions_per_hour > threshold. Integrate with Console Alerts and Slack/PagerDuty runbooks for ops.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overcommitment of nodes leads to increased preemptions and customer dissatisfaction. Mitigation: conservative default reservation packing heuristics and 'dry-run' simulator to estimate impact before enabling reservations.
Risk: Billing mismatch due to missing tags. Mitigation: require reservation id tag at the router meter and end-to-end reconciliation pipeline with nightly alerts to finance.
Risk: Complexity in UX causing misconfiguration. Mitigation: introduce sensible defaults and validation with real-time cost/impact preview in the Console.
Risk: Runtime surface performance regressions when enforcing hard isolation. Mitigation: benchmark suite and canary rollout with performance gates.
dependencies: ENG-serve: router admission API changes and reservation metadata surfaced in routing decisions
ENG-metrics: high-resolution tenant metrics and per-reservation tagging support
Billing-Infra: accept billing_multiplier dimension and hourly reservation tags
Console-UI: new reservation and SLO window management screens
Legal/Sales: contract language and pricing multipliers for pilot customers
